Coram: Hon'Ble The Chief Justice

For the Petitioner: Mr. Shailesh Kr. Singh, Advocate

For the Fci: Mr. Alok Anand, Advocate

Per M.S. Ramachandra Rao, C.J.
1.

This application is filed under section 11(6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act by the
petitioner against the respondents seeking appointment of an Arbitrator to resolve the dispute
between the petitioner and the respondents.

2.  The Respondent no.1 is MSTC Limited which is a Government Company engaged in the business of e-sale through e-auction of industrial by-products, scrap and wastage, etc. available for sale with Government and Semi Government Companies/Undertakings.
It maintains a portal which can be utilized by Government organizations for selling their services /products.
It is a mere service provider/agent of the advertiser organization.

3. Respondent no.2 is a Government of India undertaking engaged in the business of manufacture and sale of fertilizers from its factory and office situated at Sindri in the Dhanbad District of the State of Jharkhand.

4. The Respondent No.1 floated a tender inviting bids from prospective buyers for sale of Fly Ash and Bottom Ash belonging to Respondent No.2 lying in Chalk Pit Area between HURL boundary and ACC Company boundary of FCI Sindri Unit, Sindri through e-auction.
5. The portal of the respondent no.1 mentioned General terms and conditions of e-auction and M/S Absolute Vintrade Pvt. Ltd.
Having ... vs M/S Mstc Limited on 21 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155247589/
1 further buyers specific terms and conditions (BSTC).
Anenxure-1 is a copy of the BSTC which contains the arbitration clause in Clause-3.

It states:
" 3.0. ARBITRATION

In the event of any dispute or difference relating to the interpretation terms, text, application of the provisions of contracts, such dispute or difference shall be referred by either party for Arbitration to a sole Arbitrator to be appointed mutually by the parties.

In case the parties fail to appoint the sole arbitrator within 30 days of the invocation of arbitration, the same will be appointed as per the provisions of the arbitration and Conciliation Act,1996...."

6. The Petitioner became a successful bidder after participating in the e-auction and was awarded contract through issuance of a sale order dt. 26.04.2022 by the Respondent No.1, acting as agent of respondent no.2.
7.

According to the petitioner, during the execution of the work order, dispute arose between it and the respondent no.2 and so the petitioner sent a letter dt.19.1.2024 raising a dispute with the respondent no.2 requesting resolution of the same.
8. The respondent no.2 replied to the same quoting a clause relating to "INSPECTION" of the Tender and contending that they will not entertain the petitioners request.

9. Petitioner then wrote a letter dt.15.2.2024 to respondent no.2 specifically contending that the respondent no.1 ought to have agreed to resolve their dispute through arbitration and reiterating its request to resolve it through arbitration.

10. On 11.3.2024, the respondent no.2 replied to petitioner that there is no arbitration clause/
agreement in the sale order and therefore petitioners request cannot be acceded to.
11. Petitioner then got issued a legal notice dt. 12.03.2024 to both the respondents seeking appointment of an Arbitrator.

12. The Respondent no.1 sent a reply on 22.04.2024 denying the existence of dispute as well as the application of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act,1996 for the purpose of appointment of an arbitrator for settlement of dispute and shifted the responsibility to the Respondent No.2 for settlement of the dispute.
13. Therefore, the petitioner has moved this Court for appointment of an Arbitrator.

14. After service of notice in this Arbitration Application, the Respondent No.1 filed a counter affidavit contending that it should be deleted from the array of parties because it is not a necessary party quoting clauses 16.11 and 16.12 of the BSTC.

15. The said clauses state as under:

2 "Clause 16.11.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The bidder/buyer recognizes that the role of MSTC in the auction process is limited to that of a service provider/agent only and accordingly agrees not to make MSTC a party in any legal proceeding arising out of any dispute between the bidder/buyer and the seller/principal;

Clause 16.12 : The buyer acknowledges and agrees that after issuance of delivery order, as per the terms and conditions governing the e-auction, MSTC shall have no role thereafter and under no circumstances shall be held liable for any issue arising out of or related to the quality, quantity, condition, possession or delivery of the material by the sellers/principals."

16. The counsel for the petitioner sought to contend that notwithstanding the same, the respondent no.1 (MSTC) continues to be liable and should be made party to the arbitration in view of the arbitration clause referred to supra.
17.

I am unable to agree to the said contention in view of the specific provisions contained in Clauses 16.11 and 16.12 of the BSTC which limit the role of respondent no.1 only to that of a service provider and shifting the responsibility for any dispute with the Principal/FCI to the Principal only.
Petitioner

had accepted the said clauses, by registering on the e- auction portal of respondent no.1 and is therefore precluded from insisting that respondent no.1 should also be made a party to the arbitration.
18. Then the question arises as to whether there can be arbitration between the petitioner and respondent no.2 in view of arbitration clause mentioned in Clause 3 in the BSTC.
19. The General Terms and Conditions (GTC) of e-auction mentioned in the respondent no.1s portal contain in clauses 1 and 3 a requirement of registration by both the Seller and the Bidder/Buyer.

They state:
"1. WELCOME TO MSTC This unique service of auction on the internet is offered to you, subject to the following General Terms and Conditions of Service.....

In addition,
when using particular MSTC services, you and MSTC shall be subject to any Guidelines or Rules applicable to such services which may be posted from time to time.
All such guidelines or Rules are hereby incorporated by reference into the GTC.."

(emphasis supplied)
3.YOUR REGISTRATION OBLIGATIONS

In consideration of your use of the service, you agree to (a) provide true, accurate, current and complete information about yourself as prompted by the Service's registration form (such information being the "registration Data") and (b) maintain and promptly update the registration data to keep it true, accurate, current and complete.

If you provide any information that is untrue, inaccurate, not current or incomplete, or MSTC has apparent/reasonable grounds to suspect that such information is untrue, inaccurate, not current or M/S Absolute Vintrade Pvt. Ltd. Having ... vs M/S Mstc Limited on 21 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155247589/
3 incomplete, MSTC has a right to suspend or terminate your account and refuse any and all current or future use of the service (or any portion thereof).
MSTC is concerned about the safety and privacy of all its users."
20. The portal of the respondent no.1 for the instant e-auction event also indicated the Buyer Specific Terms and Conditions (BSTC), which contain the arbitration clause 3 mentioned above.
These BSTC are the guidelines or Rules mentioned in later half of clause 1 in para 17 above.
21. Thus both GTC and BSTC are binding on the respondent no.2 and the petitioner in view of clause 1 of the GTC mentioned in para 17 above.

22. Clause 22 of the General Terms and Conditions of the respondent No.1 also reiterates the same and states:
" 22.

GENERAL INFORMATION:
The GTC constitute the entire agreement between you and MSTC and the Seller/Principal and govern your use of the service, superseding any prior agreements between you and MSTC....."

23. However, the stand taken by the respondent no.2 is that it issued to the petitioner a work/sale order, filed as Annexure-A of its counter affidavit, which contains special terms and conditions and there is no arbitration clause contained in it.
24. It may be that the sale order (Annexure A to the counter affidavit of respondent no.2) given by respondent no.2 to the petitioner did not have an arbitration clause.
But the said sale order did not specifically exclude operation of the arbitration clause contained in Clause 3 of the BSTC which is the arbitration clause.

25. When it has not specifically excluded the operation of clause 3 of BSTC in the contract between itself and the petitioner, it cannot avoid the arbitration clause to which it had agreed when it registered on the respondent no.1s portal.

26. Also having utilized the e-auction portal of the respondent no.1 which contains the arbitration clause in clause 3 of the BSTC and having accepted its binding nature by registering on respondent no.1s portal, the respondent no.2 cannot contract out of any clause in the BSTC at a later point of time while issuing the sale order.

27. For the aforesaid reasons, the reference to the term party in the arbitration clause- Clause 3 means the party to the contract of sale and purchase/ sale order i.e the petitioner and the respondent no.2.

28. In this view of the matter, the application is allowed; Justice Mr. M. Karpaga Vinayagam,

4 dispute between the parties.
